label: Luke 13:1
text: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

label: Luke 13:2
text:
Jesus answered them,
“Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?

label: Luke 13:3
text: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.

label: Luke 13:4
text: Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them; do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?

label: Luke 13:5
text: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”

label: Luke 13:6
text:
He spoke this parable.
“A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it, and found none.

label: Luke 13:7
text: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down. Why does it waste the soil?’

label: Luke 13:8
text: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it, and fertilize it.

label: Luke 13:9
text: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”

label: Luke 13:10
text: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.

label: Luke 13:11
text: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and she was bent over, and could in no way straighten herself up.

label: Luke 13:12
text:
When Jesus saw her, he called her, and said to her,
“Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”

label: Luke 13:13
text: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight, and glorified God.

label: Luke 13:14
text: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”

label: Luke 13:15
text:
Therefore the Lord answered him,
“You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath, and lead him away to water?

label: Luke 13:16
text: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”

label: Luke 13:17
text: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed, and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

label: Luke 13:18
text:
He said,
“What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?

label: Luke 13:19
text: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and put in his own garden. It grew, and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”

label: Luke 13:20
text:
Again he said,
“To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?

label: Luke 13:21
text:
It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures

of flour, until it was all leavened.”

label: Luke 13:22
text: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.

label: Luke 13:23
text:
One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?”
He said to them,

label: Luke 13:24
text: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in, and will not be able.

label: Luke 13:25
text: When once the master of the house has risen up, and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside, and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’

label: Luke 13:26
text: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’

label: Luke 13:27
text: He will say, ‘I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’

label: Luke 13:28
text: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets, in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.

label: Luke 13:29
text: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.

label: Luke 13:30
text: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”

label: Luke 13:31
text: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here, and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”

label: Luke 13:32
text:
He said to them,
“Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.

label: Luke 13:33
text: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’

label: Luke 13:34
text: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that kills the prophets, and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!

label: Luke 13:35
text: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”

label: Siloam, the water quarter at southern Jerusalem
The Pool of Siloam (Second Temple period)
excavators: F. J. Bliss and A. C. Dickie (1894-97); Eli Shukron and Ronny Reich (2004- )
periods: Second Temple period; the pool reconstructed no earlier than Alexander Jannaeus (103-76 BCE)

label: Josephus on Siloam, the sweet-water fountain
author: Josephus

label: Pilate killed Galileans as they offered sacrifices
statement: Some present told Jesus that Pontius Pilate had killed Galileans while they were offering sacrifices, mingling their blood with that of their sacrifices.
note: The specific event is otherwise unrecorded. Josephus documents Pilate's lethal violence in Jerusalem (the Corban-aqueduct beating, War 2.175-177) and against the Samaritans at Gerizim (Ant. 18.85-87) but never names this event; the graph records it as a gap.

label: The tower in Siloam fell and killed eighteen
statement: A tower in Siloam fell and killed eighteen people, whom Jesus compared with 'all the men who dwell in Jerusalem'.
note: The tower is not otherwise recorded. Identification is disputed: Weill (1920) proposed a tower flanking the wall by the Pool of Siloam; Szanton (2023) showed both towers were Hellenistic in origin and rebuilt in the first century; a circular foundation c. 6 m across is believed by some to be the tower's ruins.

label: Siloam, a water source at southern Jerusalem
statement: Siloam was a place at the southern end of Jerusalem in the first century, named for its water (the pool and fountain of Siloam), where 'the men who dwell in Jerusalem' lived near.

label: A fruitless fig tree is dug around and manured
statement: In the parable a fig tree planted in a vineyard bore no fruit for three years; the vine-dresser asked to dig around it and fertilize (throw manure about) it before cutting it down - figs were cultivated in vineyards, and digging and manuring were the cultivator's remedies.

label: The bent woman straightened on the Sabbath
statement: A woman bent over and unable to straighten herself for eighteen years was healed when Jesus called her, laid his hands on her, and she stood up straight and glorified God.
note: Miracle claim written neutrally and searched honestly; recorded as none-found, as in Matthew and Mark for comparable healings.

label: The ruler of the synagogue
statement: The ruler of the synagogue (archisynagogos), indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, spoke to the crowd: there are six days for work, come and be healed on those days.

label: Untying ox or donkey to water on the Sabbath
statement: Jesus answered: does not each of you untie his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead it away to water? - Sabbath care for animals, including watering, was ordinary practice.
note: Matthew's parallel argument (12:11) uses lifting a sheep from a pit; Luke's example is untying and watering.

label: The mustard seed sown in a garden
statement: The kingdom is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his own garden, where it grew into a large tree and the birds of the sky lodged in its branches.
note: Matthew's parallel says the man sowed the seed in his field (13:31); Luke says he put it in his own garden.

label: The narrow door into the Kingdom
statement: Jesus said: 'Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in, and will not be able' - the image of a narrow entry that many seek and cannot pass once the master has shut it.
note: Matthew's parallel (7:13-14) has the narrow gate and the broad road; Luke's image is the door of a house whose master shuts.

label: 'Go and tell that fox' - Herod's threat
statement: Some Pharisees warned Jesus, 'Get out, for Herod wants to kill you'; Jesus sent back the reply, 'Go and tell that fox: I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.'
note: The Herod is Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee. The threat and the exchange are not otherwise recorded; Antipas had already beheaded John the Baptist.

label: Wikipedia: Pool of Siloam
title: Pool of Siloam
excerpt: Shukron and Ronny Reich (working with the Israel Antiquities Authority) uncovered stone steps, and it became obvious that these steps were likely to have been part of the Second Temple period pool.

label: Wikisource: Josephus, War of the Jews, Book V (Whiston)
title: The War of the Jews, Book V (Whiston)
excerpt: extended as far as Siloam; for that is the name of a fountain which hath sweet water in it, and this in great plenty also.

label: Wikipedia: Tower of Siloam
title: Tower of Siloam
excerpt: In 1920, Raymond Weill proposed that one of the towers flanking the Pilaster wall next to the Pool of Siloam could be the "Tower of Siloam." In 2023, Nacshon Szanton demonstrated that indeed both towers were constructed in the Hellenistic period, and were rebuilt in the first century.
